Where it began

Misbah-ul-Haq was born in Mianwali, in Punjab, on 28 May 1974. His parents were both school principals, and they wanted a good education for him before anything else. So while he played tape-ball cricket around his home town, he also took a degree in mathematics and physics in Faisalabad, and much later an MBA in human resource management in Lahore. Imran Khan is a distant cousin.

Cricket had to wait its turn. He made his first-class debut for Sargodha in 1998, at 24, and his first Test came in 2001.

The player

He played 75 Tests for Pakistan between 2001 and 2017, making 5,222 runs at 46.62 with 10 hundreds and 39 fifties. His best was an unbeaten 161 against India in Bengaluru.

He was a true late bloomer. Many of his finest days came after he was handed the Test captaincy in October 2010, at an age when most batsmen are thinking of the commentary box. He led Pakistan in 56 Tests, winning 26, more than any other Pakistan captain. In August 2016 his side rose to first place in the Test rankings, a spot Pakistan had not held since 1988. His last match, in Roseau in May 2017, ended in a win that gave Pakistan their first series victory in the West Indies.

What made him special

Composure was his great gift. He could play the long, patient innings, then switch in a moment to clearing the ropes. In Abu Dhabi in 2014 he reached a Test hundred off just 56 balls against Australia, matching the fastest of the time, and he also made the quickest fifty Tests had seen. One description of his batting called it orthodox-unorthodox: classical drives sitting beside a straight drive played off one knee.

If there was a gentle charge against him, it was that he took his time. Critics sometimes wished he would hurry along. He tended to answer them by winning. At Lord's in 2016, aged 42, he made a hundred and marked it with ten push-ups, a nod to his side's army training camp and a fine advert for fitness at any age.

Away from the middle

He won the 2009 World Twenty20 with Pakistan and led them to the 2012 Asia Cup. In club cricket he captained Islamabad United to the first Pakistan Super League title. Wisden named him one of its Cricketers of the Year in 2017, and he received the Pride of Performance in 2014 and the Sitara-i-Imtiaz in 2018. He also won the ICC Spirit of Cricket award in 2016.

After playing he coached Pakistan, served for a time as chief selector, and became a director of the Pakistan Children's Heart Foundation.

And finally

In one-day cricket he made 5,122 runs without ever reaching a hundred, more than anyone else has managed. It is a record that says a lot about his steadiness, and perhaps a little about his reluctance to show off.
